title: Nine Months of Waiting
subtitle: 癌症与疾病 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 癌症与疾病（生活与学习·健康医疗）
meta: 主题语境：癌症与疾病（生活与学习·健康医疗）　|　核心词汇：cancer　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cancer 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 my mother was sent to name ① a cancer she could not treat, and she said the treating was the whole of the lesson. The ② cancer, meaning the disease and not the cell, was nine months old in the notes and was watched by whoever came last; a cancer, she said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ cancer in that ward had the same chart, and the ④ cancer at the end, meaning the one the surgeon watched and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever named properly. A cancer, my grandmother said, is nine parts waiting and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the waiting is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cancer was the whole of the year, meaning the year it took and not the disease. The ⑥ cancer, meaning the year and not any of that, is the only thing in a family that everybody fears and nobody questions; a cancer, he said, is either something you name or the only word that means both a disease and a year. She said the year is the part they remember.

By 1979 the ⑦ cancer had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the waiting. The ⑧ cancer of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine months and eleven years of naming; a cancer, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cancer I remember is the one at the end, which was recorded in 1984 and is still described as the worst in the county. A ⑩ cancer, my grandmother said in 1989, is the only thing that improves by being named; every cancer, she said, is a year that has agreed to look like a disease. She said the year was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 癌症；恶性肿瘤
B. n. 癌症（指那个病本身，与细胞相对）
C. 固定搭配：name a cancer 说出癌的名称、确诊癌症
D. n. 癌症（指病房里每一例）
E. n. 癌症（指末尾那一例）
F. n. 癌症（抽象：它夺走的那一年）
G. n. 那一年（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a cancer she could not treat
The cancer, meaning the disease and not the cell
cancer was the whole of the year
the cancer had become a number in a report
The cancer of the whole thing
A cancer, my grandmother said in 1989

answers.why: name a cancer 意为“说出癌的名称、确诊癌症”，1963 年母亲被派去确诊一个她治不了的癌症。
cancer 意为“癌症”，指那个病本身而不是细胞，病历里已记了九个月，由最后走的人守着。
cancer 指病房里每一例癌症，每一例都是同样的病历表。
cancer 指末尾那一例（外科医生观察的那一例），是唯一有人认真确诊过的。
cancer 意为“癌症”，抽象指它夺走的那一年，父亲说 cancer 就是那一年的全部。
cancer 为抽象用法，指那一年本身，是一家人里人人都怕、却没人质疑的东西。
cancer 意为“癌症、恶性肿瘤”，到 1979 年这个 cancer 成了报告里的一个数字。
cancer 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九个月和十一年的确诊。
cancer 意为“癌症”，我记得的是末尾那一例，1984 年记录，至今仍被说成全县最重的。
cancer 为抽象总称，祖母说癌症是唯一会因为被说出名字而变好的东西。
